response.markdown_report:
The next experiment should test **gap-conditioned GRU retention**, after verifying padding invariance. At 30% progress, this offers a small architectural change with a clear control and avoids another combined loss-and-weighting experiment.

Three starting-point insights guide this choice. First, padding errors exceed 1e-5 in every category, so context interventions require remeasurement after correction. Second, Movies_and_TV has the highest sampled misranking rate (4.92%), but training margins cannot establish validation improvement. Third, matched prefix removal harms measured margins, so useful older context should remain available rather than being discarded indiscriminately.

Three literature insights suggest complementary directions. [MTAM](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.08598) motivates conditioning recurrent information filtering on observed gaps. [GRU4Rec’s top-k losses](https://hidasi.eu/assets/pdf/gru4rec_v2_cikm18.pdf) motivate emphasizing competitive negatives, although this does not directly address stale interests. [TedRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.18166) cautions that semantic and behavioral representations differ; title similarity alone cannot establish practical usefulness.

The resulting framework separates **state retention**, **ranking supervision**, and **item representation**. Padding correctness underlies all three; the gap is deciding when historical evidence remains useful without assuming that older events are harmful.

Scores below give originality / potential / user alignment / model alignment / implementation difficulty, each out of ten; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Assessment: positive (+), negative (−) |
|---|---|---|
| A. Gap-conditioned GRU update gate | 4/7/7/6/5 | O: +compact adaptation, −established temporal gating; P: +adaptive memory, −uncertain transfer; U: +targets stale and broad intent, −cannot infer compatibility; M: +retains useful context, −diagnostics are confounded; D: +one gate change, −timestamps and predictor integration |
| B. Uniform-pool BPR-max | 2/6/4/7/3 | O: +direct family fit, −standard loss; P: +competitive ranking, −possible false negatives; U: +stronger alternatives, −no explicit temporal mechanism; M: +targets misranking, −easy sampled diagnostics; D: +compact loss, −sampling integration |
| C. Joint title encoder inside GRU | 4/6/6/4/7 | O: +behavior-conditioned semantics, −known fusion; P: +item sharing, −sparse supervision; U: +specific descriptors, −surface resemblance risk; M: +additional evidence, −no diagnosed semantic deficit; D: +single network, −tokenization and auxiliary tuning |

**Select A.** Add a bounded, observed-gap-dependent offset to the GRU update gate, initialized at zero. This explicitly targets older interests dominating current direction and broad historical relatedness displacing specific recent choices. These are hypotheses, not demonstrated user benefits. Preserve useful historical state; do not crop histories or impose unconditional decay.

Hold the baseline loss, sampling and optimizer fixed. Compare against the padding-verified baseline using only pinned macro validation HR@10. Remeasure padding error, matched-context wrong rates and margins; neither increased sensitivity nor larger margins alone demonstrates success. Maintain one jointly trained checkpoint per category and identical predictor architecture.

idea.description: Test a single GRU4Rec whose update gate receives a bounded offset derived from observed inter-event time gaps. Initialize the added parameters to zero so the initial recurrence matches the padding-verified baseline. Keep the baseline objective, sampler and optimizer fixed to isolate temporal conditioning.
idea.motivation: The selected hypothesis explicitly addresses two observed user-facing failures: older interests remaining influential after behavior changes, and broadly related historical interests displacing specific recent matches. Adaptive gating may let the model reinterpret prior state when a new interaction arrives, while retaining durable interests. The model-facing target is context-dependent ranking robustness: matched prefix removal worsened measured margins and wrong rates, suggesting that blanket context deletion is poorly justified. All these context findings must be remeasured after padding verification. Timestamp gaps do not reveal compatibility, ownership needs, or purchase readiness.
idea.implementation_notes:
Integrate into the supplied corrected baseline; its source and exact GRU configuration were not included, so this is an implementation specification rather than a standalone train.py. Do not reconstruct its splits or preprocessing.

For PyTorch's GRU convention h=(1-z)*n+z*h_previous, add beta*tanh(g) to the update-gate preactivation, where g=log1p(max(timestamp_t-timestamp_previous,0)/86400) after converting timestamps to seconds, and beta is a trainable vector initialized to zero. The tanh bounds the gap contribution. Do not constrain beta's sign: a long gap is evidence for conditioning, not proof that memory should decay. Set the first real event's gap to zero. Record missing, invalid, and nonmonotonic timestamp counts; use a zero gap for unavailable intervals rather than inventing elapsed time. Preserve the baseline candidate-state, reset-gate, projection and scoring equations, including its dropout conventions. Verify that beta=0 reproduces the padding-verified baseline in eval mode before training.

Padding must not update recurrent state or the previous timestamp. At each position, compute the proposed state and use torch.where(valid[:, None], proposed_state, old_state); emit zero features at padding positions. Preserve aligned B x L log2feats(sequence) outputs. Read the maximum nonpadding index, never count-1, with explicit empty-history handling. Test states and candidate scores across added padding, batch permutations, empty rows and unpadded executions at tolerance 1e-5.

Timestamp-conditioned inference must preserve log2feats(sequence) compatibility. Build one train-only item-ID-pair gap lookup per category from supplied chronological training interactions: aggregate log1p elapsed-day gaps by adjacent ordered item pair and store their mean as a fixed buffer, defaulting to zero for unseen pairs. Use this same lookup in training, diagnostics and inference. This is a deterministic input feature, not a separately fitted predictor or score. It preserves the host sequence-only interface but represents a pair-level temporal proxy rather than each user's actual elapsed time; disclose that limitation. Do not train on actual per-user gaps and then silently substitute lookup gaps at inference. If the host supports an existing user-timestamp side channel consistently across all three paths, a separate experiment may use actual gaps instead; do not change the public ModelView contract.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, at most 200 epochs and 200 batches per epoch. Retain Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. DATA_DIR remains os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write all artifacts beneath the trial directory. Train on one GPU and count training, diagnostics and failures against 43,200 GPU-seconds. Preserve the baseline validation schedule and checkpoint selection, using only host macro validation HR@10 with 200 users/category, 99 unique negatives and evaluation seed 42. No hidden test access, extra datasets, pretrained weights, independent model fusion or checkpoint averaging.

Each category loads exactly one independently trained GRU checkpoint. Store temporal-feature buffers and architecture configuration with that checkpoint, and update the embedded predictor writer to reproduce the recurrence exactly. Preserve family-specific sample_batch, ModelView.model as the actual nn.Module, item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data and review_data. DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader) must return metrics and metric_definitions; diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis) must incorporate measured values and definitions. Public batches remain (None, sequence, positive, negative), each B x L. Distinguish proxy-gap strata from actual timestamp strata; unavailable measurements remain null. Preserve the twenty designated training-user full-catalog unseen-item recommendations as qualitative supporting evidence.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

# Integration sketch: inherit baseline weights, dropout, projections and scorer.
# gap_table is constructed exclusively from allowed training interactions.
# Both training and inference use the same pair-level gap features.

def temporal_gru_step(x, h, log_gap, w_ih, w_hh, b_ih, b_hh, beta):
    ir, iz, inn = F.linear(x, w_ih, b_ih).chunk(3, dim=-1)
    hr, hz, hn = F.linear(h, w_hh, b_hh).chunk(3, dim=-1)
    reset = torch.sigmoid(ir + hr)
    update = torch.sigmoid(iz + hz + torch.tanh(log_gap[:, None]) * beta)
    candidate = torch.tanh(inn + reset * hn)
    return (1.0 - update) * candidate + update * h

# beta = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(hidden_size))
# For multiple GRU layers, preserve the existing layer/dropout layout.

def log2feats(sequence):
    h = initial_zero_state(sequence.shape[0])
    previous_id = torch.zeros_like(sequence[:, 0])
    outputs = []
    for t in range(sequence.shape[1]):
        current_id = sequence[:, t]
        valid = current_id.ne(0)
        gap = train_only_pair_gap_lookup(previous_id, current_id)
        gap = torch.where(previous_id.ne(0) & valid, gap, 0.0)
        proposed = temporal_gru_step_with_inherited_parameters(
            inherited_input_embedding(current_id), h, gap)
        h = torch.where(valid[:, None], proposed, h)
        outputs.append(torch.where(valid[:, None], inherited_output_projection(h), 0.0))
        previous_id = torch.where(valid, current_id, previous_id)
    return torch.stack(outputs, dim=1)

originality.positive: A compact temporal-gating adaptation preserves the GRU family and exposes a controlled test of adaptive retention.
originality.negative: Time-aware recurrent gating is established; the pair-level timestamp proxy is primarily an interface-compatible engineering adaptation.

future_potential.positive: Could support later investigation of durable versus transient interests within one recurrent network.
future_potential.negative: No supplied experiment establishes a gain, and pair-level gaps may poorly represent individual intent changes.

code_difficulty.positive: Adds one bounded gate term and one deterministic feature buffer without introducing another predictor.
code_difficulty.negative: Faithful baseline recurrence reproduction, timestamp preprocessing, sparse pair lookup and embedded predictor consistency require careful integration.

related_work.title: MTAM (2020)
contributions: Provides a precedent for time-aware recurrent information filtering.
limitations: Does not establish gains for this compact gate modification or the pinned Amazon benchmark.
Does not validate a pair-level gap proxy as a substitute for user-specific elapsed time.

related_work.title: Recurrent Neural Networks with Top-k Gains for Session-based Recommendations
contributions: Introduces ranking objectives including BPR-max that emphasize competitive negatives in GRU recommendation.
limitations: Ranking-loss changes alone do not explicitly model temporal shifts.
Hard-negative emphasis can penalize unlabeled relevant items.

related_work.title: TedRec (2024)
contributions: Studies differences and alignment between textual and item-ID representations.
limitations: Does not establish effectiveness of a small randomly initialized title encoder inside this GRU baseline.
Textual similarity does not establish compatibility or immediate usefulness.
